correction.text: with the County of Berg beyond the Rhine (1423)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The duchy amalgamated with the County of Berg beyond the Rhine in 1423.' Berg is drawn as a 28 km circle at 7.10E 51.10N (Düsseldorf to Wipperfürth), the page gives neither area nor towns beyond Solingen. The Berg page dates the union with Jülich to 1348 in one sentence and 'after 1423' in another.

New keyframe: Berg 'in union with Ravensberg (except 1404-1437)'; the Jülich page has Ravensberg from 1437. Ravensberg is a 20 km circle at Bielefeld (8.53E 52.02N). From 1521 the four duchies Jülich, Berg, Cleves and Mark formed the United Duchies under one duke, a personal union that does not change this outline.

Ravenstein (Brabant) is not drawn. The French occupation from 1794 does not change the outline until 1801.

ledger.note: 1003: the first count of Jülich. 'The first mention of a count in the gau of Jülich in Lower Lorraine, is Gerhard I, in 1003.' The page gives no boundary.

region.text: the gau of Jülich in Lower Lorraine

ledger.note: 1356: Jülich becomes a duchy. 'In 1356 Emperor Charles IV of Luxembourg raised William V to the rank of duke.'

1423: Berg joins Jülich. 'The duchy amalgamated with the County of Berg beyond the Rhine in 1423'; the Berg page says 'The County of Jülich united with the County of Berg in 1348' and elsewhere 'after 1423 in union with the duchy of Jülich'. Berg had been a duchy since 1380 ('in 1380 the Emperor Wenceslaus elevated the counts of Berg to the rank of dukes').

region.text: the County and Duchy of Berg beyond the Rhine

ledger.note: 1437: Ravensberg. The Berg page lists Berg 'in union with Ravensberg (except 1404-1437)'; the Jülich page has Ravensberg 'from 1437'. The county's earlier union with Berg is not dated on either page.

region.text: the County of Ravensberg round Bielefeld

ledger.note: 10 June 1609: the Treaty of Dortmund. After Duke John William died on 25 March 1609 without heirs, the claimants Brandenburg and Neuburg signed the Treaty of Dortmund and set up a provisional joint government; they were 'also known as the possessors'. Archduke Leopold took Jülich for the Emperor on 23 July 1609.

region.text: the United Duchies' lands of Jülich, Berg and Ravensberg

ledger.note: 23 July 1609: Leopold takes Jülich. 'On 23 July, von Rauschenberg transferred Jülich to Archduke Leopold', whom the Emperor had sent to take the city.

region.text: the city and fortress of Jülich

ledger.note: 1 September 1610: Jülich falls. The Protestant army began the siege on 29 July 1610 and 'On 1 September, the garrison surrendered in return for free passage into Upper Alsace.'

region.text: the city and fortress of Jülich

ledger.note: 12 November 1614: 'Eventually, the Treaty of Xanten was approved on 12 November 1614.' Dutch troops had ejected the Neuburg garrison from Jülich in May 1614 and Spinola's Spanish army had taken Neuss, Mülheim and Wesel after the capture of Aachen in August.
12 November 1614: Xanten gives Ravensberg to Brandenburg. 'Cleves-Mark and Ravensberg went to George William of Brandenburg.'

12 November 1614: the Neuburg line takes the duchies. 'The territories of Jülich-Berg and Ravenstein went to Wolfgang Wilhelm of Neuburg' (Palatinate-Neuburg); the dynasty changes inside the state. Neuburg inherited the Electoral Palatinate in 1685 (Berg page) and Düsseldorf became the Palatine residence in 1690.

1742: the Sulzbach line. The Neuburg line 'had died without issue in 1742, Count Charles Theodore of Palatinate-Sulzbach' succeeded; 'after 1777 also Duke of Bavaria' (a personal union with Bavaria that does not change the territory).
1794: France occupies Jülich. 'In 1794 Revolutionary France occupied the Duchy of Jülich.'

region.text: the Duchy of Jülich west of the Rhine

ledger.note: 1801: the French occupation of Jülich ends in annexation (Treaty of Lunéville).
1801: 'The Treaty of Lunéville in 1801 officially acknowledged the cession of Jülich to France.'
15 March 1806: Berg becomes a grand duchy. Infobox 'Elevated to Grand Duchy: 15 March 1806'; 'Berg became the Grand Duchy of Berg, under the rule of Napoleon's brother-in-law, Joachim Murat'.

wars.name: War of the Jülich Succession
wars.outcome: Duke John William died on 25 March 1609; the claimants held the duchies jointly as 'possessors', Jülich was besieged and taken on 1 September 1610; in 1614 the Dutch and Spanish intervened and the Treaty of Xanten (12 November 1614) gave Jülich-Berg and Ravenstein to Neuburg and Cleves-Mark and Ravensberg to Brandenburg; the Treaty of Cleves (1666) 'significantly reduced the conflict'.
wars.note: The Cleves page does not mention a 1666 treaty and has Cleves 'finally incorporated into Brandenburg-Prussia' in 1666.

certainty.note: The pages give counts, dukes and towns, not boundaries.
The 12 November 1614 Treaty of Xanten divides the duchies by name, not by line; the 1666 treaty is not on the pages.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Jülich or Berg row (Grand Duchy of Berg is 1806 on).

SCOPE. One state for Jülich and Berg: the Jülich page's infobox, Berg's union in 1423 (the Berg page also says 1348). The County of Berg itself (1101, duchy 1380) before the union is not drawn: no dossier for duchy-of-berg 1101-1423 exists. The United Duchies of Jülich-Cleves-Berg (1521-1614) are a personal union of this state with duchy-of-cleves and are not territory (rule 4); the electorate-of-brandenburg dossier names them `julich-cleves-berg` as the counterpart of its 1614 gain: the Cleves-Mark part is this batch's duchy-of-cleves, the Ravensberg part is the loss recorded here.

SHAPES are circles (gazetteer lacks the towns): Jülich 6.37E 50.93N 32 km; Berg 7.10E 51.10N 28 km; Ravensberg (Bielefeld) 8.53E 52.02N 20 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Jülich', 'Düren', 'Bielefeld' (radius places); 'Berg' / 'Bergisches Land' (region).

NOT SETTLED. (1) No area on either page. (2) Berg's first union with Jülich: 1348 or 1423. (3) Ravensberg's earlier union with Berg is undated. (4) Ravenstein (Brabant) went to Neuburg in 1614 and is not drawn; Brandenburg gave up its claim in 1671 (JS page). (5) The 1614 occupations: the Dutch and Spanish held Cleves, Mark, Wesel, Neuss and Mülheim in 1614 without dates on the page; not entered. (6) The French annexation of Jülich: 1794 occupation, Lunéville 1801 (no month on this page). (7) From 1685 the Neuburg line also held the Electoral Palatinate, from 1777 Bavaria; both are personal unions (electoral-palatinate dossier has the 1685 Neuburg gain of the Upper Palatinate district).

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: duchy-of-berg (1101-1423), county-of-ravensberg, palatinate-neuburg, julich-cleves-berg (as an umbrella, 1521-1614).
